import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/test_3.csv"
]

# List to hold dataframes
dfs = []

# Load each source CSV file with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# All source tables have the same schema and the target schema is a subset of source schema (only 'TrackID')
# According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, we can UNION all source tables on the common columns and then project 'TrackID'

# Concatenate all source dataframes (union)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Select only the 'TrackID' column as per target schema
target_df = combined_df[['TrackID']]

# Remove duplicate TrackID rows to match the target examples (which show unique TrackID values)
target_df = target_df.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

# Ensure TrackID is integer type as per target schema
target_df['TrackID'] = target_df['TrackID'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file without the index column
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
